notes.title: Kelvin Ren · Personal profile
notes.markdown:
# Kelvin Ren
Kelvin is 34, uses he/him pronouns, and lives in Shanghai with his partner Yiwen and a cat called Tofu. He runs Clockless, a three-person studio building Worldlet, the Mac app where Fox lives.

## Home
Partner: Yiwen Su, a product manager at a hospital-scheduling company. Parents: in Chengdu, arriving {{parentsArrive}} for a week. Cat: Tofu, eight, opinionated about breakfast.

## What matters now
- Ship Worldlet 0.36 on {{launch}} with the Applet stages in it and the stage-exit crash gone.
- Walk into the Northwind meeting on {{investorMeeting}} with the numbers Sam asked for.
- Choose between Ruth and Omar for the designer role by {{day:designerDecision}}.
- Give the Tokyo Dev Summit talk on {{talkDay}}, then rest two days in Kyoto.
- Have the flat ready before Mum and Dad arrive.

## Preferences
Short answers, amounts in USD, the tradeoff before the decision. One main thing per day. Evenings belong to Yiwen and a run by the river. Never book, pay or message anyone without being asked.

This person, his company, his contacts and every record in this world are fictional. Email addresses use example.com.

Related: [[How I like to work with Fox]] · [[Yiwen Su · Family rhythms]] · [[Worldlet 0.36 · Release plan]]

notes.title: How I like to work with Fox
notes.markdown:
## Working with Fox
Say what is waiting, not everything that exists. Group by the thing I am doing, not by the app it came from.

- Mornings: what is on today and the one thing that would hurt to miss.
- Before a meeting: the people, the last thing we said to each other, the number they asked for.
- Evenings: nothing, unless a flight or a person is involved.

When I ask for a decision, show me the two options and the difference between them, then wait. Never send a message, book a room or move money on your own.

## Issue #208 · clockless/worldlet
Leaving the Mail stage while a letter is still rising closes the app. Reproduces on three of four pilot Macs.

Steps: open Mail, pick a letter, press Back before the sheet finishes rising.

Findings so far: the stage is disposed while its animation still holds a reference to the renderer target. Jay has a fix that cancels the tween on exit; needs a test that drives the click on the canvas.
